title: Why static main methods are hidden rather than overridden
answer: No. The standard `main` method is `static`, and static methods are not overridden in Java because overriding is based on runtime polymorphism for instance methods. A subclass may declare another static method with the same signature, but that is method hiding, not overriding. The method selected depends on the class through which the static method is referenced or, for Java application startup, the class name passed to the launcher. Adding `@Override` to a static `main` method in a subclass causes a compile-time error because there is no instance-method override relationship. So a subclass can hide a parent class's static main method, but it cannot override it polymorphically.
